text.p: AirTouch Communications Inc., the diversified cellular and paging operator, said Thursday its profits jumped 74 percent in the second quarter as revenues grew even faster despite rising competition.
The company said its net income for the three months ended June 30 soared to $106 million, or 21 cents a share, from $61 million, or 12 cents a share in the year-ago quarter.
The per-share results were far better than Wall Street had expected. The consensus had been for 14 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
The company's stock shot up $2.50 to $31 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. It was one of the most actively traded issues on the NYSE.
AirTouch said its revenues for the quarter raced ahead by 87 percent to $901 million from $481 million as it added 617,000 new customers.
"Without a doubt this is the best quarter we've ever had," Chairman Sam Ginn said.
Ginn said that, based on the company's results so far this year, AirTouch was on track to meet or exceed its goal of $1.5 billion in cash flow for 1997.
AirTouch said second-quarter operating cash flow profit margins grew to 35.6 percent from 30.8 percent a year ago.
The company said its net income for the first half of the year rose to $170 million, or 34 cents a share, from $113 million, or 23 cents a share in 1996.
Revenues also expanded by 87 percent in the half to $1.74 billion from $930 million.

AirTouch said the addition of 617,000 cellular, personal communications services and paging customers allowed it to reach more than 9 million customers, including AirTouch's proportionate ownership in various domestic and international properties.
"With our international start-ups reaching profitability and our U.S. cellular margins at an all-time high, we are well-positioned for the remainder of the year," Ginn said.
